newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice prices on upswing - traders.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice prices on upswing - traders.

text.p: Vietnamese rice prices are on an upswing amid increased demand and with farmers withholding stocks in the hope of pushing prices higher, traders said on Thursday.
Five percent broken grade rice was quoted at around $280-$285 a tonne FOB Saigon Port, compared with $275-$280 a week ago. Twenty-five percent broken grade was trading at around $215-$220 a tonne.
"The farmers are looking to create a phoney rice fever," said one trader. "But I expect next week the prices will go down."
Dealers said Sri Lanka remained a significant buyer of lower grade rice. African markets and companies in South Korea were also reported to be interested in Vietnam rice.
Heavy flooding in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta was continuing to have some impact on the market through delays in transportation and milling.
But traders said a government decision last month to raise Vietnam's rice export quota to 3.2 million tonnes has had no apparent effect on prices.
Vietnam sold 2.025 million tonnes of rice to overseas buyers last year, making it the world's fourth largest exporter of the grain after the United States, Thailand and India.
